method: Fix size first: median |reaction| from anchors, scaled up when 20d realised vol runs hot versus that history. Direction only where an asymmetry exists that is not already legible: positioning versus run-up, or a structural payout mechanic. Widely-covered mega-caps with a well-formed consensus default to Neutral. Call Neutral whenever the directional case rests on macro narrative alone or |score| would sit under 15.
key_drivers: Reaction base rate is tiny and sign-balanced: median 1.63%, max 4.14%, 4 up / 4 down
Staples sector carrying tariff, commodity and FX drag; peer P&G posted flat organic sales
CL at ~24x forward on negative (-5.9%) recent earnings growth, a premium multiple on shrinking EPS
Already de-rated 7.6% off the 52w high; 20d run-up -1.25%, so little sell-the-news setup
20d realised vol 26.6% is high for CL, arguing for a slightly wider move than the 1.63% median
what_would_change_my_mind: An organic-sales or margin datum specific to CL's oral-care and Hill's mix that consensus had not already absorbed.
reasoning: Nothing here is hard-won. The staples headwind, the tariff drag and CL's premium multiple on flat earnings are all thoroughly published, so they sit in the price. The base rate is the dominant fact: eight reactions with a 1.63% median and no sign skew. Elevated 20d vol argues for a slightly wider distribution than history, hence 2.2% rather than 1.63%. The mild negative tilt reflects valuation and sector direction, not a specific edge, and is small enough that Neutral is the honest label.

key_drivers: Preliminary AUM $1.79T with $9bn long-term net INFLOWS - the outflow story that capped BEN has inverted
Beat in each of last four quarters, average 19%; positive Earnings ESP into this print
S&P +15% over the April-June quarter mechanically lifts fee revenue; consensus 66c is +34.7% y/y
Reaction base rate is up-skewed and large: +6.86, +2.86, +7.04, +10.37 among the last seven
Offset: only -3.7% from the 52w high and +56.6% off the low, so much of the recovery is banked
what_would_change_my_mind: Evidence that the inflow figure came with adverse mix or that comp and distribution expense is eating the operating leverage the market has extrapolated.
reasoning: My rule discounts legible evidence, and the preliminary AUM is monthly-disclosed and therefore priced. But two things survive that discount: a four-quarter beat streak averaging 19% against a positive ESP, and a reaction distribution that is genuinely up-skewed when flows improve. The unknown is margin, not revenue, and BEN has repeatedly surprised on it. Against that, the stock sits near its 52w high after a 57% recovery, which caps how much good news is still unpriced. That tension yields a modest lean rather than a strong call, with size set at the 4.39% median.

key_drivers: 20d realised vol 137.7% annualised implies ~8.7% daily moves - the 6.08% median badly understates size
Reaction history is left-skewed: 5 of 8 negative, downside tails -28.2%, -13.9%, -8.0%
Stock spiked ~+14% on 21 Jul to ~110 then gave it all back; 20d run-up -15.5%, -37% from 52w high, which lowers the bar
New CFO effective 5 Aug, two days after the print - outgoing team delivers the guide, transition adds uncertainty
Positive read-through from strong LRCX/AMAT results and China capacity buildout, but that is fully legible
what_would_change_my_mind: A gross-margin or Semiconductor-segment mix datum showing UCTT converting the WFE upcycle into operating leverage rather than passing it through.
reasoning: No news corpus exists for this name, so the call rests on filings, nine StockTwits messages and the price record. The one thing I am confident about is size: vol at 137% annualised means a 6% move is an ordinary day, and the print should produce something near 11%. Direction genuinely cancels. The left-skewed reaction history and the CFO handover argue down; the 15.5% give-back into the print and strong customer results argue up. UCTT's failure mode is margin, not revenue, and I cannot read margin from here. Neutral with a whisper of negative skew is the honest answer.

key_drivers: Reaction base rate small and mildly up-skewed: median 1.75%, 5 of 8 positive, only one move beyond 3%
The swing factor is the quarterly distribution declaration, not EPS - a mineral-rights LP trades on payout
20d run-up +11.15% and within 2.5% of the 52w high already discounts the commodity strength
That run-up creates sell-the-news risk if the distribution merely holds rather than rises
Most recent reaction was the worst of the set at -3.86%, so the prior bar was reset lower
what_would_change_my_mind: A distribution declaration materially away from the prior $0.32, in either direction, or a hedge-book disclosure that caps participation in the gas rally.
reasoning: Thinnest corpus of the four: three StockTwits messages and no news read. That caps evidence quality, not the call. BSM is a distribution-mechanics name with a tight reaction distribution, and the two forces offset cleanly. Commodity strength and a low bar after May's -3.86% print argue up; an 11% twenty-day run-up into the 52w high means that strength is already paid for, so a merely-maintained payout disappoints. Vol at 20.9% is unremarkable, so I hold size near the 1.75% median with a small bump for commodity sensitivity. No directional edge worth naming.
